3	/// Every decision the call framing makes, as a pure reducer — the one part of
4	/// the LiveCommunicationKit integration a test can hold, because the framework
5	/// itself cannot be stood up off a device (`RobotCallController` is the thin
6	/// adapter over it, untested by design the way `WebRTCDataChannel` is).
7	///
8	/// The model the user chose (issue #78): a call *starts* when the microphone is
9	/// unmuted — "call the robot" is literally what opening the camera tab and
10	/// unmuting is. Muting during a call does not end it (an ordinary in-call
11	/// mute); the call ends from an End button — the system UI's or the app's own,
12	/// which are one funnel — from the session becoming ineligible (robot asleep,
13	/// stream failed, viewport target gone), or from a manager reset. Passive
14	/// viewing is never a call.
15	///
16	/// The invariant every path holds: **the microphone is live only while a call
17	/// is active.** Each ending effect list carries `.applyMic(false)`. The one
18	/// deliberate exception is a start the *system* refused (`startFailed`): the
19	/// framing is garnish and the microphone is the meal, so the mic opens bare —
20	/// see that case for the reasoning.
21	struct CallLifecycle: Equatable, Sendable {
22	    enum State: Equatable, Sendable {
23	        case idle
24	        /// A start was requested; the permission ask and the system's
25	        /// `StartConversationAction` round trip are in flight.
26	        case starting
27	        case active
28	    }
29	
30	    private(set) var state: State = .idle
31	
32	    /// Why a call ended without the user asking, in the vocabulary the system
33	    /// call UI understands.
34	    enum EndCause: Equatable, Sendable {
35	        /// The stream failed under the call.
36	        case failed
37	        /// The far side went away on its own terms — the robot slept, was
38	        /// disconnected, or the viewport target dissolved.
39	        case remoteEnded
40	    }
41	
42	    enum Event: Equatable, Sendable {
43	        /// The mic button (or a redial) asked for the microphone.
44	        case unmuteTapped
45	        /// The mic button asked for silence.
46	        case muteTapped
47	        /// The permission ask came back refused.
48	        case micPermissionDenied
49	        /// `ConversationManager.perform` threw before the system took the start.
50	        case startFailed
51	        /// The system delivered the `StartConversationAction` for us to do.
52	        case performedStart
53	        /// The system delivered a `MuteConversationAction` (its own UI and the
54	        /// in-app button arrive identically — one funnel).
55	        case performedMute(isMuted: Bool)
56	        /// The red button beside the microphone, inside the app.
57	        case endTapped
58	        /// The system delivered an `EndConversationAction`.
59	        case performedEnd
60	        /// The session under the call went away: robot asleep, stream failed,
61	        /// or no viewport target left.
62	        case sessionBecameIneligible(EndCause)
63	        /// `conversationManagerDidReset` — everything is already torn down.
64	        case managerReset
65	    }
66	
67	    /// What the adapter must now do, in order. Reporting is separate from
68	    /// fulfillment on purpose: fulfilling an `EndConversationAction` *is* the
69	    /// end signal, so `performedEnd` carries no `.reportEnded` — only endings
70	    /// the system did not initiate are reported.
71	    enum Effect: Equatable, Sendable {
72	        /// Hand audio-session ownership to the call (`MediaAudioSession`),
73	        /// before the start is fulfilled — the CallKit contract's ordering.
74	        case takeAudioOwnership
75	        /// Ask for the microphone permission; granted continues into the
76	        /// system start, refused comes back as `.micPermissionDenied`.
77	        case requestMicPermissionThenStart
78	        /// Route an in-call mute change through the system so its UI stays in
79	        /// step (`MuteConversationAction`); the change lands via
80	        /// `performedMute`.
81	        case performMuteAction(isMuted: Bool)
82	        /// Route the in-app End through the system (`EndConversationAction`),
83	        /// so the button beside the microphone and the one on the Lock Screen
84	        /// are one funnel; the ending itself lands back via `performedEnd`.
85	        case performEndAction
86	        /// Actually flip the microphone track.
87	        case applyMic(Bool)
88	        /// Fulfill the system action currently being performed.
89	        case fulfillPendingAction
90	        /// Refuse the system action currently being performed.
91	        case failPendingAction
92	        /// Tell the system the outgoing conversation is on its way. Reported
93	        /// back-to-back with `.reportConnected`, legitimately: a call can only
94	        /// start from a stream already up (`CameraMicButton` is disabled until
95	        /// `.streaming`), so there is no connecting interval to wait out.
96	        case reportStartedConnecting
97	        case reportConnected
98	        case reportEnded(EndCause)
99	        /// Donate the start-call intent so Recents redial and Siri suggestions
100	        /// have something to hand back.
101	        case donate
102	    }
103	
104	    mutating func handle(_ event: Event) -> [Effect] {
105	        switch event {
106	        case .unmuteTapped: unmuteTapped()
107	        case .muteTapped: muteTapped()
108	        case .micPermissionDenied: startAbandoned()
109	        case .startFailed: startFailed()
110	        case .performedStart: performedStart()
111	        case let .performedMute(isMuted): performedMute(isMuted: isMuted)
112	        case .endTapped: endTapped()
113	        case .performedEnd: performedEnd()
114	        case let .sessionBecameIneligible(cause): becameIneligible(cause)
115	        case .managerReset: managerReset()
116	        }
117	    }
118	
119	    /// The permission was refused: the start never happened, nothing was
120	    /// reported, and the mic must stay shut — there is nothing to undo.
121	    private mutating func startAbandoned() -> [Effect] {
122	        guard state == .starting else { return [] }
123	        state = .idle
124	        return []
125	    }
126	
127	    /// The *system* refused or lost the start — `perform` threw, the action
128	    /// timed out, or no robot identity was known. Permission is already
129	    /// granted by the time a start can fail this way, so the microphone opens
130	    /// bare: the user asked to talk to the robot, and a button that silently
131	    /// does nothing because the call *framing* was refused is the bug this
132	    /// case exists to end (shipped once — the whole chain swallowed failures
133	    /// and the tap read as dead). The controller logs the reason; a later
134	    /// unmute simply tries the framing again.
135	    private mutating func startFailed() -> [Effect] {
136	        guard state == .starting else { return [] }
137	        state = .idle
138	        return [.applyMic(true)]
139	    }
140	
141	    private mutating func performedStart() -> [Effect] {
142	        guard state == .starting else { return [.failPendingAction] }
143	        state = .active
144	        return [
145	            .takeAudioOwnership, .fulfillPendingAction, .applyMic(true),
146	            .reportStartedConnecting, .reportConnected, .donate,
147	        ]
148	    }
149	
150	    private mutating func performedMute(isMuted: Bool) -> [Effect] {
151	        guard state == .active else { return [.failPendingAction] }
152	        return [.applyMic(!isMuted), .fulfillPendingAction]
153	    }
154	
155	    /// The app's own End. It asks the *system* rather than ending here, for the
156	    /// reason `muteTapped` does: the Lock Screen's button and this one must be
157	    /// one funnel, or the two UIs disagree about whether a call is up. The
158	    /// ending arrives back as `performedEnd`.
159	    ///
160	    /// `.starting` is refused rather than queued — there is no conversation for
161	    /// the system to end yet, and the button is not on screen in that phase
162	    /// (it is gated on `activeCall`, which fills at `.active`).
163	    private mutating func endTapped() -> [Effect] {
164	        guard state == .active else { return [] }
165	        return [.performEndAction]
166	    }
167	
168	    /// `.starting` accepted too: the system can end a call it is still
169	    /// validating.
170	    private mutating func performedEnd() -> [Effect] {
171	        guard state != .idle else { return [.failPendingAction] }
172	        state = .idle
173	        return [.applyMic(false), .fulfillPendingAction]
174	    }
175	
176	    private mutating func becameIneligible(_ cause: EndCause) -> [Effect] {
177	        guard state != .idle else { return [] }
178	        state = .idle
179	        return [.applyMic(false), .reportEnded(cause)]
180	    }
181

**Assessment**

- **Logging (SENSITIVE-TO-OBSERVABILITY)**: The new `Self.log.notice/error` statements interpolate `uuid` (random `UUID()` per call — not identity), `String(describing: error)` (LiveCommunicationKit framework errors — internal enum types), `String(describing: cause)` (`.failed`/`.remoteEnded` enum), `isMuted` (bool), and `lifecycle.state` (internal enum). - **`voip` UIBackgroundMode**: Legitimate entitlement for `ConversationManager.perform`. No PushKit registration is added (`reportNewIncomingConversation` still uncalled), so no incoming-call attack surface. Background execution is scoped to an active conversation — not a standing privilege.

- **`endCall()` and lifecycle `endTapped`**: Gated on `state == .active`; refused when `.starting` or `.idle`. State machine ends fail-CLOSED — `performEndAction`'s catch path invokes `sessionBecameIneligible(.remoteEnded)`, which drives the mic off (`applyMic(false)`) and clears `activeCall`. No path leaves the mic live after failure.

- **`keepsSessionAlive` = `lifecycle.state != .idle`**: Set after every effect run, and every terminal event (`startAbandoned`, `startFailed`, `performedEnd`, `becameIneligible`, `managerReset`) resets state to `.idle`. - **`ConversationDelegateAdapter` extraction**: Was `private` in the same file, now internal in the same package. Not exposed cross-module; class initializer still only called from `ensureManager()`. No visibility widening across trust boundaries.

- **`RobotCallController.preview(...)`**: Gated by `#if DEBUG`. Not compiled into release. Writes only to `activeCall` with a synthetic `"preview-robot"` id.

- **`CameraSession.preview` `isMicEnabled` parameter**: Inside `#if DEBUG` extension. No production reachability.
